dependency_asset_review: Installed candidates were reviewed from the controller catalog (`/work/dependency-assets.json`; 97 candidates, all under the single installed distribution pyhmmer). All are packaged `pyhmmer/tests/data` fixtures matching only by the "LuxC" stem. Findings: (1) `pyhmmer/tests/data/hmms/txt/LuxC.hmm` — a prebuilt profile HMM. I compared it byte-for-byte against the HMM the analysis actually produces: the 1,204 emitted model-body lines and all remaining header lines (NAME/ACC/LENG/NSEQ/EFFN/CKSUM/GA/TC/NC/STATS) are identical; the only differences are the transient HMMER3 version banner, a DATE timestamp, and an added COM line. This is the precomputed scientific content of the LuxC.hmm endpoint, so I declared its removal in `dependency-exclusions.json` (sha256 e7a4dd57c83fb17cc12640f20c4f02f126d8230b16d6c6ef596bf791c8075865); the second controlled test confirmed removal of exactly that one file and the analysis still completed successfully with both endpoints produced. (2) `pyhmmer/tests/data/seqs/LuxC.faa` — this is the analysis input itself (sha256-identical to the staged `/inputs/seqs/LuxC.faa`); a copy that is exactly the given input is not a precomputed answer, so I left it installed rather than deleting input data. No domtbl-format LuxC search-result fixture exists in the wheel (the only .domtbl files are PF02826/RREFam/A0A089QRB9 outputs of other HMMs). Other stem matches (`msa/LuxC.sto` input copy, `msa/LuxC.weighted.sto` — a per-column reweighted variant of the alignment, `msa/LuxC.faa` — a different 12-sequence FASTA, `msa/LuxC.hmmalign.sto` — an hmmalign output for other tools, `msa/LuxC.sto.ssi` — an SSI index) are alternate inputs or intermediate-format fixtures, not serialized forms of either endpoint; I did not remove them. Residual uncertainty: this was targeted inspection guided by the priority matches, not an exhaustive semantic audit of all 400 distribution files, and I did not inspect fixtures unrelated to the LuxC stem.
explanation: The pyhmmer `msa_to_hmm` example was set up and executed offline in two controlled tests, both passing (exit 0). Inputs are the original notebook data files: the notebook's `docs/examples/data` is a symlink to `src/pyhmmer/tests/data` in revision 90d2f28, so `data/msa/LuxC.sto` and `data/seqs/LuxC.faa` were staged from the resolved raw.githubusercontent URLs (sha256 e2cf20e9… and 7ce47aae… respectively, recorded in inputs.json and re-verified by the controller). The unchanged scientific script built the LuxC Plan7 profile HMM from the 13-sequence Stockholm alignment (NAME LuxC, ACC PF05893.5, LENG 400, NSEQ 13) and searched the 12-sequence LuxC.faa protein database, producing both exports: LuxC.hmm (187,150 bytes) and LuxC.domtbl (4,093 bytes, 12 domain-hit rows). The second test additionally applied one declared exclusion (the bundled precomputed LuxC HMM test fixture) and still completed with both artifacts present. The runtime is roughly 0.3 s, far within limits.
source_adaptations: analysis.py: the two file open statements for MSAFile("data/msa/LuxC.sto") and SequenceFile("data/seqs/LuxC.faa") were changed to "/inputs/msa/LuxC.sto" and "/inputs/seqs/LuxC.faa" because the notebook's relative data directory does not exist in the offline reference working directory. No other statements, imports, comments or scientific logic were altered; the staged files carry the exact bytes the notebook's symlinked data directory resolves to at the pinned revision.
unresolved_assumptions: The exported LuxC.hmm contains a DATE timestamp line and a COM build line emitted by hmmbuild at serialization time, so its exact sha256 differs between runs (and between my two controlled tests) even though the model body and all other header fields are byte-stable. Any later grading must not rely on a byte-identical LuxC.hmm hash; comparing the model body or the domtbl output is stable.

The repository's LICENSE copying states MIT for the repository; the LuxC.sto alignment and LuxC.faa sequences are Pfam/UniProt-derived test data whose independent redistribution terms were not established beyond the repository's MIT licensing claim. Staged data stayed within the sandbox.

A byte-identical copy of the LuxC.sto input also ships inside the installed pyhmmer wheel at pyhmmer/tests/data/msa/LuxC.sto (and LuxC.faa at tests/data/seqs). These are given inputs rather than answers, so they were intentionally not excluded; a task design that treats central storage of the input as leakage would need to stage the inputs from elsewhere.
